proposals.before: I would punish poseurs who feign sainthood and bring down slanderers like Zang Cang;
proposals.after: I would punish Li Chu for posing as a sage and bring down slanderers like Zang Cang;
proposals.reason: Chinese names 犁鋤 as a specific person; idiomatic "poseurs" erases the personal name parallel to Zang Cang.

proposals.before: Then I would shut my gate to study moral teaching and read Confucius and Laozi, hoping for something of the immortals' ease; I would climb the Long ridges and high hills, send my spirit wandering through heaven and earth, and let my eyes sweep the eight reaches of the world.
proposals.after: Then I would shut my gate to study moral teaching and read Confucius and Laozi, hoping for something of the blessing of [Chisongzi] Song and Wangzi Qiao; I would climb the Long ridges and high hills, send my spirit wandering through heaven and earth, and let my eyes sweep the eight reaches of the world.
proposals.reason: Chinese 松、喬 names the immortals Chisongzi and Wangzi Qiao; idiomatic reduces them to generic "immortals".

decisions.after: I would punish Li Chu for obstructing the sage and chastise Zang Cang for slandering the wise;
decisions.reason: 誅犁鋤之介聖兮，討臧倉之訴知 names Li Chu parallel to Zang Cang, so erasing 犁鋤 as generic "poseurs" is wrong; but 介聖 means interposing against / obstructing the sage, not posing as one, and 訴知 is Zang Cang's slander of the wise.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 誅犁鋤之介聖兮，討臧倉之訴知

decisions.after: Then I would shut my gate to study moral teaching and read Confucius and Laozi, hoping for something of the blessing of Chisongzi and Wangzi Qiao; I would climb the Long ridges and high hills, send my spirit wandering through heaven and earth, and let my eyes sweep the eight reaches of the world.
decisions.reason: 庶幾乎松、喬之福 names the immortals Song/Chisongzi and Qiao/Wangzi Qiao and seeks their 福 (blessing), so "immortals' ease" erases the names and mistranslates 福; the proposal's bracketed "[Chisongzi] Song" is still awkward for idiomatic English.

claimRevisions.reason: The truncated English name "Li" does not match 犁鋤; revising r0001 restores the full personal name Li Chu.
松 in the pair 松、喬 is Chisongzi, not "Prince Song"; the princely title belongs to Wangzi Qiao, and revising r0002 restores the correct religious name.
